thread:
maya: Heads up — helm chart lint keeps failing in CI for `redis-inference` chart. Locally `helm template` + chart-testing passes, but CI chart-build errors with a panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference when templates reference `.Values.gpu.nodeSelector`. Our helper `common.nodeSelector` assumes `.Values.gpu` exists.

ben: Seen this before. Helpers assume `.Values.gpu` shape. We used `required` elsewhere which is brittle. Quick guard is `{{- if and (hasKey .Values "gpu") .Values.gpu.enabled }}` but that's ugly.

oscar: Pro tip: normalize with `default` at start of template: `{{- $gpu := default dict .Values.gpu }}` then use `$gpu.enabled` and `$gpu.nodeSelector`. That avoids nil panics.

maya: Did that but CI still crashed. Chart-testing in CI renders a matrix including `values-legacy.yaml` which sets `gpu` to the string `"auto"` for legacy clusters. Our helper's `$gpu.enabled` looks up `.enabled` on a string and panics. We need the lint/render matrix to include legacy shapes and a safe coercion pattern.

liam: We should add a render-matrix job: run `helm template` with `--values` set to minimal, full, legacy, and gpu-enabled variants. Also add `helm-unittest` cases for `common.nodeSelector` to assert empty map when not present.

deploy-bot: chart-lint #342 FAILED: helm template redis-inference returned non-zero exit code. Logs: https://ci.redwood.example/ci/342

ben: Another approach is a strict `values.schema.json` that declares `gpu` as an object with `enabled:boolean` and `nodeSelector:object`. Chart-testing would then reject legacy values early. Problem: breaking change for GitOps and older clusters.

oscar: You can do `oneOf` in JSON Schema to accept either `object` or `string` and then coerce in templates. Helm's schema validator supports `oneOf`/`anyOf` depending on helm version — test it. But safer is to normalize in templates using `kindOf`/`default`. Example: `{{- $gpu := dict }}{{- if eq (kindOf .Values.gpu) "string" }}{{- /* legacy */ }}{{- else }}{{- $gpu = .Values.gpu }}{{- end }}`.

maya: Also saw a production fallout this morning: rollout automation created a DaemonSet with `nodeSelector: { gpu: "true" }` but cluster labels use `accelerator="nvidia-t4"`. Pods stuck Pending, cluster-autoscaler spun up generic nodes, cost spiked. We need standardized label mapping in chart values + a helper `helpers.mapAcceleratorLabel` that maps from logical `gpu` to provider labels.

liam: Good call. I'll draft a PR that: a) adds the render-matrix to CI, b) updates helpers to use `default` coercion patterns, c) introduces `values.schema.json` with backward-compatible `oneOf` and migration notes, d) adds a small mapping helper and doc snippet.

liam: PR opened (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/789 — PTAL @maya @ben

maya: Also add an acceptance step that runs `helm template` with our `argocd-values.yaml` (simulate ArgoCD rendering) to catch env-drift. And add a short README section about label conventions and migration.

ben: Agree — also flip on `helm lint --strict` in CI so schema violations fail fast.

oscar: One more nit: we used `required` in a few helpers which causes helm to error at render time if missing. Replace with safe checks and reserve `required` for intentional hard failures in charts where missing means misconfiguration.

maya: Assigning this to @liam. I'll merge once unit tests and render-matrix pass. Thanks all :pray:
